name: RDPEGFX Remaining Refactor Work
description: Ralph-ready loop for remaining RDPEGFX refactor work. The loop removes backend RDPEGFX PDU replay from production viewer output, finishes moving viewer-local RDPEGFX protocol state out of viewer_server.c, keeps canonical framebuffer output authoritative, hardens caps/ACK/reset/resize behavior, and records final validation evidence. Backend replay must not be moved into another production module and no deprecated/test-only replay path may be linked into production binaries.

userStories.title: Add frame epoch and backpressure-safe ACK handling
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want frame IDs paired with epochs and bounded byte-based pacing so stale ACKs and slow viewers cannot corrupt dirty pacing across reset, resize, reconnect, or 32-bit frame ID wrap.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-viewer GFX epoch is incremented on baseline reset, resize, reconnect, and session reset.
Dirty in-flight map stores frame ID, framebuffer generation, epoch, timestamp, and queued/sent byte accounting needed for backpressure.
ACK handling rejects frame IDs from old epochs.
Frame ID wrap from UINT32_MAX to a valid next frame ID is explicit and tested.
ACKs from pre-wrap/pre-reset/pre-resize frames cannot unsuspend or advance dirty pacing state.
Byte-based GFX backpressure prevents unbounded in-flight dirty payload bytes per viewer.
Tests cover stale ACKs, wrap, reset/resize/reconnect epochs, byte-limit denial, and byte accounting cleanup on ACK/reset.

userStories.notes: Completed: Viewer GFX dirty frames are keyed by frame epoch and frame ID, ACK-invalidating reset/invalidation/baseline/wrap boundaries increment epoch and clear frame/byte state, frame ID 0 remains reserved, stale/unknown nonzero ACKs no longer update accepted ACK state or dirty pacing, and a conservative internal 4 MiB per-viewer dirty byte limit gates sends until current-epoch ACKs release bytes. Stale ACKs from old dimensions/epoch are ignored.
